questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of women's football in England
The rules and history of the Cricket World Cup
How to become a professional footballer as a teenager
Why football is shown on TV more than other sports
questions.why: Catherine says they'll find out about the history of women's football in England.

questions.q: What has Sam enjoyed about this Women's World Cup?
options: Playing in some of the matches herself
Watching the games live on TV and the media interest
Going to the stadium in France almost every day
Betting on the results with her friends at work
questions.why: She says it's great to watch the matches live on TV and there's so much media interest.

questions.q: According to Gemma Clarke, what has happened after each success of women's football?
options: More money was given to the sport by the government
The players became famous and very well paid
There was a backlash and efforts to hold women back
Men's football became less popular for a few years
questions.why: She says there has been a backlash and an attempt to keep women back.

questions.q: What does Gemma Clarke say women footballers have struggled to do?
options: Find enough players for their teams
Travel to matches in other countries
Learn the rules of the modern game
Be taken seriously as athletes
questions.why: She says it has been a struggle 'to be taken seriously as athletes'.

questions.q: How popular was women's football during and after the First World War?
options: Crowds of up to 50,000 watched games
Only a few hundred people watched
It was only played in schools
It was more popular in other countries
questions.why: Catherine says crowds of up to 50,000 were watching games.

questions.q: What did the Football Association do?
options: Paid women players the same as the men
Started a new national women's league in 1921
Banned women from its grounds for about 50 years
Asked the best women to join the men's teams
questions.why: Gemma Clarke says they banned women from association grounds for about 50 years.

questions.q: Why were the men who ran the game worried, according to Catherine?
options: Women were getting badly injured during matches
The pitches were getting damaged by too many games
Women's games might take money and fans from men's
Women didn't follow the rules and argued with referees
questions.why: She says they thought it might take money and supporters away from the men's game.

questions.q: When was the ban finally lifted?
questions.why: Catherine says the ban was lifted comparatively recently, in 1971.
